entities.summary:
Berardo Eroli (1409–1479) was an Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a significant role in the Church during the late Middle Ages. 

As a prominent cleric, Eroli was involved in several key events, including the Council of Pisa (1409) and the Conclave of 1473, which led to the election of Pope Sixtus IV. 

Eroli's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he contributed to the development of the Catholic Church's canonical laws and helped shape the Church's relationships with the emerging nation-states of Europe. 

His life was marked by a series of remarkable appointments, including his elevation to cardinal in 1467 and his appointment as bishop of Pavia in 1473. 

One of Eroli's most lasting contributions was his role in the translation of the Bible into the vernacular languages of Europe, a project that would go on to shape the course of Western literature and culture.
